title: Ordinary colimits assembled over a directed cover of the index category
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$, and call sets and categories small when they belong to it. Let $I$ be a small nonempty poset such that every finite subset has an upper bound. Let $C$ be a small ordinary category and $(C_i)_{i\in I}$ full subcategories, with literal inclusions $C_i\subseteq C_j$ for $i\leq j$, such that every object of $C$ belongs to some $C_i$. A full subcategory contains every morphism of $C$ between its objects. Let $\mathcal A$ be an ordinary category with small Hom sets and all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and let $F:C\to\mathcal A$ be a functor. Choose colimit cocones $(L_i,(\lambda_{i,c})_{c\in C_i})$ for $F|_{C_i}$ and $(L,(\lambda_c)_{c\in C})$ for $F$. For $i\leq j$, let $u_{ij}:L_i\to L_j$ be the unique map satisfying $u_{ij}\lambda_{i,c}=\lambda_{j,c}$ for every $c\in C_i$, and let $v_i:L_i\to L$ be the unique map satisfying $v_i\lambda_{i,c}=\lambda_c$. Then the maps $u_{ij}$ define an $I$-diagram, and $(L,(v_i))$ is a colimit cocone on it. More precisely, for every $H\in\mathcal A$, taking the composites with $\lambda_{i,c}$ gives a bijection between families $f_i:L_i\to H$ satisfying $f_j u_{ij}=f_i$ and cocones $(g_c:F(c)\to H)_{c\in C}$ on $F$; it sends $g_c$ to the unique $f_i$ with $f_i\lambda_{i,c}=g_c$ on $C_i$. The comparison $\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}L_i\to L$ induced by the $v_i$ is therefore an isomorphism with these specified legs. Empty $C$ and empty members $C_i$ are allowed.

source.place: Agent-formulated directed-cover assembly lemma from Categories Definition 002F (definition-colimit, lines 1310-1329). Tag 002F supplies the universal property, not a separately numbered directed-cover assertion; directedness is explicitly defined in the statement. The argument extracted from former Step 12 of lem-coef-cellular-tree-presentable-approximations is recorded in report.md.

proof.text: For each $i\leq j$, the legs $\lambda_{j,c}:F(c)\to L_j$ for $c\in C_i$ form a cocone on $F|_{C_i}$, because $C_i$ is full and $C_i\subseteq C_j$. The universal property of the chosen colimit $L_i$ therefore gives a unique $u_{ij}:L_i\to L_j$ with $u_{ij}\lambda_{i,c}=\lambda_{j,c}$. Comparing composites with all $\lambda_{i,c}$ proves $u_{ii}=1$ and $u_{jk}u_{ij}=u_{ik}$ whenever $i\leq j\leq k$, so these maps form an $I$-diagram. The same universal property gives the unique $v_i:L_i\to L$ with $v_i\lambda_{i,c}=\lambda_c$, and comparison on the same legs gives $v_ju_{ij}=v_i$.

source.place: Categories, Definition 002F (label definition-colimit), universal property; directed-cover argument supplied here.

proof.text: Given a compatible family of maps $f_i:L_i\to H$ with $f_ju_{ij}=f_i$, define a map $g_c:F(c)\to H$ by choosing $i$ with $c\in C_i$ and setting $g_c=f_i\lambda_{i,c}$. This is independent of the choice: for two such indices, choose an upper bound $k$; then both expressions equal $f_k\lambda_{k,c}$ by compatibility and the definition of $u$. If $a:c\to d$ is a morphism of $C$, choose one index containing $c$ and $d$; the finite-upper-bound hypothesis supplies it, and fullness puts $a$ in that $C_k$. The cocone equation for $\lambda_{k,-}$ then gives $g_dF(a)=g_c$. Thus $(g_c)$ is a cocone on $F$.

source.place: Categories, Definition 002F (label definition-colimit), universal property; directed-cover argument supplied here.

proof.text: Conversely, let $(g_c:F(c)\to H)$ be a cocone on $F$. For each $i$, its restriction to $C_i$ is a cocone on $F|_{C_i}$, so the colimit property gives a unique $f_i:L_i\to H$ satisfying $f_i\lambda_{i,c}=g_c$. For $i\leq j$, the composites $f_ju_{ij}$ and $f_i$ agree after every leg $\lambda_{i,c}$, hence are equal by uniqueness. These two constructions are inverse: starting with $(f_i)$ recovers each $f_i$ by uniqueness on the legs, and starting with $(g_c)$ recovers every $g_c$ by choosing an index containing $c$. Therefore compatible families $(f_i)$ are in bijection with cocones on $F$.

source.place: Categories, Definition 002F (label definition-colimit), universal property; directed-cover argument supplied here.

proof.text: The preceding bijection is natural in $H$. By the colimit universal property for the $I$-diagram $i\mapsto L_i$, compatible families of maps $f_i:L_i\to H$ are exactly maps from its colimit to $H$. Under the bijection, this family maps to the cocone $(g_c)$, and the corresponding arrow has composites $v_i$ on the $L_i$-legs because $v_i\lambda_{i,c}=\lambda_c$. Hence $(L,(v_i))$ itself satisfies the universal property of a colimit of the $I$-diagram. The canonical comparison from a chosen $\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}L_i$ to $L$ is consequently an isomorphism, uniquely characterized by those legs.

source.place: Categories, Definition 002F (label definition-colimit), universal property; directed-cover argument supplied here.

proof.text: If $C$ is empty, every $C_i$ is empty and the same argument says that all relevant colimit cocones are initial and the unique-family bijection is the singleton bijection. If some $C_i$ is empty, its colimit is likewise initial, but the constructions above use only the universal property and remain unchanged. Thus the stated empty cases require no extra hypothesis.

lean.statement: theorem ordinary_directed_cover_colimit {I : Type u} [PartialOrder I] [Nonempty I] (hdir : ∀ i j : I, ∃ k : I, i ≤ k ∧ j ≤ k) {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (S : I → ObjectProperty C) (hmono : Monotone S) (hcover : ∀ c : C, ∃ i : I, S i c) {A : Type v} [Category.{u} A] [HasColimitsOfSize.{u, u} A] (F : C ⥤ A) (s : ∀ i : I, Cocone ((S i).ι ⋙ F)) (hs : ∀ i : I, IsColimit (s i)) (t : Cocone F) (ht : IsColimit t) : ∃ (D : I ⥤ A) (e : ∀ i : I, D.obj i = (s i).pt) (v : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj t.pt), (∀ (i j : I) (hij : i ≤ j) (a : (s i).pt ⟶ (s j).pt), (∀ c : (S i).FullSubcategory, (s i).ι.app c ≫ a = (s j).ι.app ⟨c.obj, hmono hij c.obj c.property⟩) ↔ a = eqToHom (e i).symm ≫ D.map (homOfLE hij) ≫ eqToHom (e j)) ∧ (∀ (i : I) (a : (s i).pt ⟶ t.pt), (∀ c : (S i).FullSubcategory, (s i).ι.app c ≫ a = t.ι.app c.obj) ↔ a = eqToHom (e i).symm ≫ v.app i) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit (⟨t.pt, v⟩ : Cocone D)) ∧ (∀ H : A, ∃ E : { f : ∀ i : I, (s i).pt ⟶ H // ∀ (i j : I) (hij : i ≤ j), (eqToHom (e i).symm ≫ D.map (homOfLE hij) ≫ eqToHom (e j)) ≫ f j = f i } ≃ (F ⟶ (Functor.const C).obj H), ∀ (g : F ⟶ (Functor.const C).obj H) (i : I) (c : (S i).FullSubcategory), (s i).ι.app c ≫ (E.symm g).val i = g.app c.obj) ∧ IsIso (colimit.desc D (⟨t.pt, v⟩ : Cocone D)) ∧ (∀ i : I, colimit.ι D i ≫ colimit.desc D (⟨t.pt, v⟩ : Cocone D) = v.app i)
